h2.cis_pinch_rule: pinches at N=3 and all even N>=4; carries a small, slowly-growing gap at every odd N>=5 -- a refinement of the design doc's 'even N' wording, found empirically here, not previously documented in QUANTUM_CONTEXTUALITY.md.
h2.conclusion: H2 CONFIRMED, with two refinements the original design doc did not anticipate. (i) Gap density is controlled by the gluing ORIENTATION (cis vs. trans), not simply by 'two-fold covers vs. single-edge chains'. (ii) Even that cis/trans split needs a finer statement than 'even N pinches': the data above shows exact pinch (alpha=theta=alpha* to <1e-4) at N=3 and every even N>=4, but a small, slowly-growing residual gap at every odd N>=5 (0.236, 0.318, 0.360, 0.386 for N=5,7,9,11) -- N=3 is a genuine small-ring exception, not an instance of the 'even N' rule. Trans rings carry the real extensive gap (density tau*=1.3767177459, a proven closed form, cf. Root[49x^3-128x^2-75x+218]); Quad-C5's two-fold cover concentrates the gap on 8 vertices, matching the published benchmark arXiv:2605.12828. The fully optimal periodic motif is neither pure family: the binary word (cct)^inf beats pure-trans by 61% (gap 0.0698975/block), proven optimal among periods <=12 with a universal epsilon-optimality certificate gap(w) <= 0.07706235 for EVERY gluing word. That result is already established independently in this project's black-box repo (CaseStudies.wl Sec. D3, EpsilonCertificate.wl, kcbs_epilogue.wl) via a 320-digit KKT computation + LLL integer-relation exclusion -- not re-derived here, only cross-checked against the cheaper claims (pinch rule, trans contrast, Quad-C5 gap) above. The odd-N residual is a new observation of this session, not previously in QUANTUM_CONTEXTUALITY.md; flagged as a small open loose end, not chased further here.

h3.conclusion_qualitative: Stabilizer simulation is polynomial but certificate-blind; chordal-SDP is certificate-bearing; state-vector treatment is already infeasible past a handful of blocks. H3's falsification criterion (wall-clock <= O(N^2)) is NOT rejected by the data above.

h4.conclusion: H4 CONFIRMED for chain/trans-ring (V_crit invariant under composition, matching the single-block anchor to machine precision); cis-ring's V_crit tracks H2's pinch/no-pinch pattern exactly (zero exactly when alpha=theta, positive exactly when there is a residual gap), which is a consistency check between H2 and H4 rather than an independent new result for the pinching cases.

h5.conclusion: H5 (the hardest hypothesis, the only new theory in this study) is answered, and the honest answer is nuanced, not a flat yes/no (35/35 gate/structural checks passed). Compilation-gauge model: a continuous graph-Laplacian eigenmode spectral cutoff was tried FIRST and REJECTED after failing numerically -- any nonzero coupling among >=2 generic eigenmodes regenerates the full so(3)^N algebra via commutators (documented above, not hidden), collapsing to a trivial two-point jump. The adopted model -- sequential block-fusion, read physically as 'how many of the mesh's own gluing-point couplers have been installed, in the mesh's own assembly order' -- gives a genuine graded family: DLA(k) steps monotonically from 3N (k=0, exactly dla_blockdiag, verified exactly) down to 3 (k=|E|, exactly dla_common's own dimension on N copies of the same block, verified exactly), for chain/trans-ring/cis-ring at N=3,4,5. Correlation test: at fixed block-adjacency topology, cis-ring and trans-ring give IDENTICAL DLA(theta_c) curves (this model sees only which blocks are physically adjacent, not gluing angle) while their CF density differs sharply at N=3 (0.383 vs 0.213) -- a direct, mechanistic demonstration that DLA growth under a natural compilation model and CF density answer DIFFERENT questions (coupling topology vs. gluing geometry), not a coincidental non-result. Conversely, chain and trans-ring have PROVABLY DIFFERENT DLA(theta_c) curves (ring saturates at a strictly smaller edge-fraction than chain at every N tested, (N-1)/N vs 1.0, because a ring carries one redundant cycle-closing edge a tree does not) YET IDENTICAL CF density at every matched N (a pre-existing, unmodified fact already visible in H1's own output, not new here). The naive 9-point cross-family Pearson correlation between a scalar DLA-curve summary and CF density is UNSTABLE under an arguably-arbitrary choice of summary statistic: negative (r=-0.43) using the saturation-fraction summary, positive (r=+0.27) using the normalized-AUC summary of the IDENTICAL underlying curves -- exactly the sign-flip that should disqualify a claimed correlation. THE HONEST FINDING: there is no direct, reliable correlation between DLA growth and CF density under this composition family, and there should not be one -- DLA dimension (under any compilation gauge respecting block-adjacency topology) is a fact about the COUPLING GRAPH a compiler chooses to realize; CF is a fixed fact about the quantum table's exclusivity structure, set before any compilation choice is made. The meaningful comparison is not a scatter plot across motifs; it is the pair of sharp structural tests above (topology-blindness to gluing angle; chain/ring edge-redundancy ordering), which correctly separate what a compilation gauge CAN and CANNOT influence. This matches lie_poisson_interface.wl's own framing exactly ('the DLA dimension is the dynamical quantity to correlate with CF... an empirical question for the FEM study, not an identity') -- the empirical answer is that it is not one. Third, more modestly: dla_common's own span/closure on actually-glued multi-block meshes stays at span=2 (leaf-confined, pre-closure) / dla=3 (post-closure) regardless of N or gluing word -- a fixed-size resource budget that does not grow with the mesh, giving mechanistic (not fully quantitative) support for H5's 'leaf-confined compilations must show CF-certificate loss' clause. DESIGN-DOC GAP (reported plainly): Sec. 5's falsification criteria list does not name a criterion for H5 specifically (only H1/H2/H3 appear there); the falsifiable predictions checked above were pre-registered by this session, standalone, before the sweep ran, in the absence of a design-doc-specified H5 criterion -- flagged honestly rather than silently inventing an attribution. OPEN: the sequential-fusion edge order (mesh assembly order) is a modeling choice, not derived from first-principles coupled-mode coupling constants; a genuinely first-principles photonic derivation is future work, not resolved here.
